note: Vocabulary and tool names used by scripts/pab_literacy_shift.py to score assistant behaviour from PatientAgentBench transcripts. Lives in data/ because this repo's convention is that domain vocabulary never appears in Python source. Nothing here is imported from PatientAgentBench: the tool names are observed in this study's own transcripts and re-declared, the same way data/pab_transcript_contract.json re-declares the arm grammar.
status_note: The escalation and reassurance term lists are a first pass by the study author and have NOT been reviewed by a clinician. Any figure or number derived from them must carry the draft label, exactly as the urgency tiers do (data/urgency_tiers.draft.json). They are deliberately coarse: presence of a term is evidence a topic was raised, not a judgement that the advice was right.

workflow_tools.note: Tool names observed in the run transcripts. completion_tools are the ones whose successful call means the patient left the conversation with something booked; lookup_tools mean the assistant went to the sandbox for facts rather than answering from the prompt.

escalation_terms.note: Language that routes the patient toward faster or higher-acuity care. Matched case-insensitively as whole words/phrases against assistant text only.

reassurance_terms.note: Language that routes the patient toward slower or lower-acuity care, or that closes the concern without a care action.

self_care_terms.note: Advice the patient can act on alone. Counted separately from reassurance: telling someone to rest is not the same as telling them their symptom is not serious.
